title: Static tile instruction stream with compiled dependencies
summary: Flatten cross-operator tiles into a replay stream and encode dependency formulas or counters beside the stream. This is a strong fit for regular, fixed-shape programs where host compilation can eliminate most runtime scheduling decisions.

title: Task/event runtime with device-ready queues
summary: Persistent scheduler and worker roles turn dependency events into ready tasks. The design handles dynamic order and imbalance but must explicitly budget scheduler SMs, queue traffic, atomics, and fences.

title: Role-specialized communication/compute MegaMoE
summary: Assign persistent workers to dispatch, scheduling, expert compute, gather, and combine; use token/tile readiness to overlap network movement with tensor-core work and remove stage-wide barriers.

title: Choose static replay or a dynamic ready runtime
summary: Use static replay when shapes and dependency structure are stable and launch/synchronization overhead dominates. Use an event/ready runtime when routing, arrivals, or workload size change enough that precomputed order leaves substantial bubbles.
conditions: Measure shape stability and task-duration variance.
Account for scheduler SMs, atomics, fences, and runtime waits.
Check whether a hybrid static graph plus limited dynamic readiness is sufficient.
recommendation: Start from the least dynamic scheduler that satisfies the workload; add device-side dynamic choice only for observed uncertainty.
alternatives: Static monolith for a very small fixed model.
PDL or CUDA Graph when modular kernels already perform well.
non_applicable: Do not choose a dynamic queue solely because it sounds more general.
Do not claim static replay supports arbitrary continuous batching without evidence.

title: Make multi-die topology part of scheduling and signaling
summary: On GPUs with private per-chiplet caches, place related tiles on the same chiplet and aggregate completion locally before publishing global events. Flat SM load balancing can trade nominal balance for cache thrashing and fabric synchronization.
conditions: Private cache or memory-scope domains exist.
Related tasks reuse weights or state within that domain.
Local and global signaling primitives are available.
recommendation: Use chiplet-local gangs/queues and local counters, with one aggregated global publish per completed local share.
alternatives: Static per-XCD partitioning when task sizes are fully known.
non_applicable: Do not transfer MI350 XCD counts or memory-scope instructions directly to B300.

title: Choose a one-kernel MegaMoE or a streaming multi-kernel pipeline
summary: A one-kernel design is compelling when role partitioning and readiness remove stage barriers without starving expert compute. A streaming multi-kernel design is preferable when modular optimized GEMMs, independent stream scheduling, or maintenance boundaries dominate.
conditions: Compare dispatch, expert, gather, and combine timing boundaries.
Estimate communication/compute SM partition and tail imbalance.
Check whether symmetric-memory and cooperative-residency assumptions are acceptable.
recommendation: Select the boundary that minimizes critical-path bubbles, not merely launch count.
alternatives: StreamEP-style tile streaming across persistent kernels.
Split backend under the same serving API.
non_applicable: Do not label a communication-only dispatch/combine library as a complete MegaMoE.
Do not compare training and serving results without matching topology and timing scope.

title: Expose a compact schedule IR to the kernel-design agent
summary: Separate handler implementation from task graph, worker placement, dependency, memory lifetime, and dispatch configuration. Let the agent search the schedule IR first and lower to device code through a compiler/runtime contract.
conditions: The runtime has reusable task handlers.
Schedule choices can be validated before full code generation.
The evaluator distinguishes faithful runtime transfer from standalone speed.
recommendation: Use typed fields for tasks, dependencies, worker roles, placement, memory lifetimes, and topology; record each candidate as an evidence-bearing episode.
alternatives: Direct CUDA/PTX generation for a tightly scoped handler.
Static monolith generation for a tiny fixed model.
non_applicable: Do not let the agent rewrite the entire runtime for every candidate.
Do not promote an IR candidate on a standalone metric that misranks runtime behavior.

title: A persistent single operator is not automatically a MegaKernel
summary: Persistence is the launch substrate, not the classification criterion. A persistent GEMM or attention remains single-operator unless its resident scheduler also crosses operator, model-stage, or communication-stage boundaries.
label: non-megakernel
missing_criterion: No cross-operator or cross-stage task boundary is established.

title: PDL, CUDA Graph, and streaming persistent kernels are adjacent alternatives
summary: These approaches can reduce host gaps and expose fine-grained overlap while preserving separate kernel boundaries. Classify them by actual launch semantics and evaluate them as legitimate alternatives.
label: adjacent-infrastructure
missing_criterion: Multiple device kernels remain distinct rather than sharing one resident multi-stage execution substrate.

title: Whole-generation and near-whole-model boundary contrast
summary: model-as-a-kernel closes prompt consumption, LM head, greedy argmax, and token feedback in one persistent launch. qwen_megakernel keeps embedding/layers/final norm in its main kernel but launches LM head and argmax separately.

title: Equivalent device-resident substrates across CUDA, NKI, Pallas, and Ascend
summary: The defining property is device-resident multi-stage scheduling, not CUDA syntax. NKI Transformer TKG, Pallas Fused EP MoE, and Ascend mixed-core MegaMoE paths qualify through their invocation and stage boundaries, with hardware-specific scheduling semantics.

title: DeepGEMM MegaMoE lineage and backend reuse
summary: Treat the original DeepGEMM MegaMoE, its TIRx port, and FlashInfer backend integration as one related lineage for deduplication and train/test splitting, while preserving their implementation-stack differences.
